newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Rexrodt urges prompt EMU start.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Rexrodt urges prompt EMU start.

text.p: German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Wednesday it was vital for European monetary union (EMU) to start on time in 1999, and any delay could lead to "irritations" on international financial markets.
In a speech to bankers in Berlin, Rexrodt said that the launch of the euro was needed in order to deepen the European integration process and give it a new dimension.
He said EMU was also vital to anchor the monetary stability already achieved by European countries, to boost competition, increase price transparency and cut business costs.
"That is why January 1, 1999 must remain the starting date for the common currency," Rexrodt said, according to the text of the speech he was due to give.
Rexrodt added it was wrong to pursue a political debate over delaying the euro, because the postponement could turn out to be permanent and there could be a new rise of protectionism.

"But it would be just as wrong to create a currency union at any price for political reasons, while losing sight of economic good sense," Rexrodt said. "If we get it wrong economically, then political integration would suffer too.

"An unstable currency would be a heavy price for Europe. We do not face a choice between sticking to the timetable or softening the criteria -- we must meet the challenge of meeting the criteria," Rexrodt said.

The German government has set a target of cutting its budget deficit to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product this year -- just below the three percent ceiling set by the Maastricht treaty governing EMU.
Rexrodt said that the publication of new tax revenue forecasts next week would "show exactly where we stand" on meeting that goal. But he said he did not want to anticipate the figures.
